catalog_description: Experiments comparing a control against one or more variants, with the success metric and run duration tracked.
Account-based marketing campaigns aimed at specific target accounts across multiple channels.
Per-worker running balances for a leave type: accrued, taken, scheduled, and available, reset each accrual cycle.
Worker requests for time away (vacation, sick, parental, bereavement, jury duty), carrying eligibility, approval chain, and accrual deduction.
Accessibility violations found by automated scans, with severity, the guideline broken, the affected page, and remediation steps.
Customer requests to open a deposit or payment account, covering account type, initial funding, linked services, and identity verification.
Account or contact marketing engagement scores reflecting in-market propensity, derived from intent and activity signals.
Resolutions of anonymous web and signal traffic to a known account or contact.
An account's progression through orchestration stages, from early awareness through to an opportunity.
Records of newly opened deposit or payment accounts, with account number, type, customer, funding method, and activation date.
Fit and priority scores per account, derived from the ideal customer profile and segment model for planning.
Time buckets within a fiscal year, with open, soft-close, closed, or locked status that drives period-end close.
Team or manager commitments to act on engagement survey results, tracked through to closure.
Configurable rules that decide which captured activities count toward which opportunity or account for engagement and attribution reporting.
Raw operational measurements (energy, fuel, waste, mileage) used to calculate emissions.
Targetable audience definitions (custom, lookalike, saved interest, or suppression lists) synced to one or more ad platforms.
Budget assignments and pacing for a campaign or ad set, including caps, reallocation decisions, and the resulting spend split over time.
Accounts or audiences targeted by an account-based ad campaign, with their channel and tier.
Conversion and signal events sent server-side to an ad platform and matched back to paid delivery for optimization and attribution.
Reusable creative building blocks (images, video, headlines, copy, logos, CTAs) stored for assembly into ads and variants.
Product catalog feeds used to drive dynamic product ads, mapping catalog fields to creative templates per platform.
FCRA-mandated notices issued when a background check is used to decline a candidate, covering the pre-adverse and post-adverse two-step process and dispute window.
Records linking advocacy-share-driven traffic to a lead, opportunity, or pipeline value for social-selling attribution and program ROI.
Time-boxed advocacy pushes that group content around a launch, event, or theme and set participation targets for advocates.
Curated, approved content items made available to advocates to reshare, with suggested copy and a sharing window.
Topic channels that group advocacy content by theme so advocates can follow and filter the subjects relevant to them.
Personalized digests of shareable content sent to advocates to prompt participation, built from each advocate's opted-in topics.
Ranking boards of advocates by points, shares, reach, or earned media value over a period, used to recognize and motivate participation.
Append-only ledger entries recording points awarded to or redeemed by an advocate for a specific action.
Configured employee advocacy programs, holding the enrolled audience, content topics, sharing rules, branding, and goals.
Rewards in the advocacy catalog that advocates redeem with earned points, with cost and redemption lifecycle.
Per-share engagement measurements: clicks, impressions, reactions, comments, reach, and earned media value for an employee share.
Individual acts of an employee resharing advocacy content to a linked personal social account, with channel, timestamp, and any personalized copy.
Personal social network accounts that advocates have connected and authorized for one-click resharing.
Employees enrolled as advocates, with participation status, opted-in topics, gamification standing, and linked social accounts.
Influence scores for advocates, derived from network size, engagement rate, reach, and share performance over a window.
Seed, fertilizer, chemical, and fuel stock across farm bins and sheds, reconciled against applications and purchases.
Pre-engagement client estimates priced from rate cards, expected effort, and media or production costs, which convert to a job once approved.
Central engagement records for agency clients, the unit of billable work, carrying the brief, deliverables, assigned team, and rolled-up financials.
Recurring fee agreements with a client, covering the monthly amount, included scope, and live burn-down against logged time and costs.
Records of a staffing or search agency submitting a candidate against a requisition, with the dedup ownership window and fee terms on conversion to a hire.
Time logged against an agency job, task, and deliverable, with rate-card application, billable coding, and discipline tagging.
Contact-center agent presence, availability, and pause-code state transitions.
Deliverable units of work below an epic, sized to be completed within a program increment by one or more teams.
Long-lived teams-of-teams that plan and deliver a continuous flow of value on a common cadence.
Time-phased views of planned epics and features across upcoming program increments, used for release planning and stakeholder communication.
Registered LLM agents and generative-AI workflows, with prompt templates, tool bindings, retrieval indexes, evaluation harness, and deployed endpoints.
Noise-reduction rules defining which alert patterns to filter or suppress, such as known-noise signatures and maintenance exclusions.
Per-product-line allergen maps with changeover validation, labeling controls, and supplier-attestation references.
Veterinary patients (companion animals, livestock, equine), with species, breed, identifying marks, microchip, and ownership history.
Sale or purchase transactions for animals or mobs, with counterparty, head count, weights, price, and destination.
Vaccinations, treatments, and medicine administrations for an animal or mob, with product, batch, dose, and the withholding period that gates sale eligibility.
Weigh observations for an animal or mob, with weight, date, and source, used to compute average daily gain and growth curves.
Detected deviations from learned normal behavior, such as KPI excursions, novel error patterns, or traffic shape changes.
Runtime registrations of API consumers, covering API key provisioning, assigned scopes, quota allocation, and on/off toggle.
Runtime instances of an API version, tracking which version runs where (production, staging, regional) and its rollout and canary state.
Gateway infrastructure for APIs, with deployment targets and throughput configuration.
Rules governing API access, transformation, rate limits, and authentication.
API schemas (OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL) that define the interface contract published for consumers.
Aggregate API metrics per version and consumer: call counts, latency percentiles, and error rates.
API version lineage (v1.0, v2.0, sunset dates), each with its own policies, deployments, and audience.
OFCCP-mandated logs of every internet applicant against a requisition, capturing demographics, expressed interest, qualifications, and disposition for audit.
Aggregated total cost of ownership per enterprise application: license fees, infrastructure, support, personnel, and cloud usage.
Categorized reasons a job application was not selected, driving OFCCP applicant-flow reporting and internal hiring analytics.
Named integration points between two applications (API, ETL, message queue, file-drop, manual), with payload type, data owner, frequency, and SLA.
Candidate answers to screening questions on a specific job application, used to auto-disqualify on knockout rules.
Custom screening questions attached to a job posting or template, including knockout and qualifying questions with their answer type and rules.
Audit-trail records of an application moving between stages, with from-stage, to-stage, actor, timestamp, and reason for cycle-time analytics.
Configured stages in the recruiting pipeline (sourced, applied, screened, onsite, offer, hired) that define a job application's lifecycle.
Multi-dimensional time-series scores per application: criticality, revenue attribution, adoption, strategic alignment, and technical health.
Reader satisfaction signals on knowledge articles: ratings, helpful or not-helpful votes, and comments.
Audit trail of edits to a knowledge article, with prior version, author, timestamp, change summary, and revert capability.
Stock-based compensation expense recognized per period per cohort of grants, with forfeiture and modification accounting under ASC 718.
Lease-accounting journal entries posted to the general ledger under ASC 842 or IFRS 16, covering recognition, amortization, interest, modification, and termination.
Per-learner, per-attempt records of an assessment: start time, score, pass or fail, and time on task, retained as compliance evidence.
Item-bank questions with their stem, answer choices, scoring, and metadata for randomization.
Lease, maintenance, support, or warranty contracts governing an asset or pool of assets, indexed on the asset side.
Per-asset, per-book depreciation timelines giving period-by-period expense and accumulated depreciation, driving the monthly depreciation entries.
Cross-cutting lifecycle log for hardware, software, and SaaS assets: procurement, deployment, transfer, retirement, and disposal.
Management-fee schedules and performance-fee waterfalls for general partners, required to calculate true limited-partner returns.
Forecasts of voluntary and involuntary attrition over a planning horizon, broken down by org unit, tenure, performance band, and geography.
Defined customer cohorts (high-value-active, churn-risk, holiday-shoppers) computed from events and attributes, activated for targeting and outreach.
Dynamic learner segments defined by attributes like department, location, and role, used by auto-enrollment and notification rules.
Scoped audit fieldwork initiatives, with scope statement, budget, team, timeline, and procedures, moving from planned to completed.
Control deviations, process gaps, or non-compliance found during audit fieldwork, with condition, cause, impact, remediation owner, and target date.
Identified gaps, risk exposures, or non-conformances from assessments, audits, or policy exceptions, with priority, due date, owner, and status.
Multi-year audit strategies and annual calendars defining audit-universe coverage, risk-based scoping, and timing.
Forward-looking corrective-action proposals from audit fieldwork, with risk rating, proposed owner, target date, and expected cost or benefit.
Formal audit deliverables, with executive summary, scope, findings and recommendations ranked by severity, management response, and sign-off.
Rule-engine entries that auto-enroll learners into courses or paths based on audience membership and lifecycle events.
Reusable remote-execution scripts in a management tool's library, with version history, parameter schema, scheduled runs, and per-target outcomes.
Human review decisions on a completed background check (clear, engaged, decisional, declined), with rationale and individualized assessment notes.
Individual sub-check results inside a background check order (county criminal, SSN trace, employment verification, drug screen), each with its own status and source.
Candidate-initiated disputes of a background check result under FCRA, with the disputed component, candidate statement, re-investigation result, and resolution.
Configured bundles of check types that can be ordered as one unit, defining what a standard package looks like for a role tier.
External verification results for a candidate (criminal, employment, education, credit, identity), with status and findings from a screening provider.
Owned cash or operating accounts at a bank, with institution, account number, currency, and intended use, driving cash management and payment runs.
Customer banking issues, disputes, and escalations (unauthorized transactions, fraud claims, account errors, complaints), with account, agent, SLA, and resolution.
